FROZEN_DERIVATION_RULES.kind: 'drizzle-migration'. Derived from the unit's directory: db/migrations/NNNN_*.sql is the drizzle chain (db/hosted/baseline-manifest.ts BaselineUnitKind). Not 'supabase-migration' (supabase/migrations/*.sql) and not 'policy' (db/policies/NNN_*.sql).

FROZEN_DERIVATION_RULES.ordinal: The next contiguous integer after the current maximum. At START_HEAD that is 79. Re-derived, never assumed.
FROZEN_DERIVATION_RULES.dependsOn: IDS, never ordinals — 'an insertion in the middle must not silently re-point a dependency at a different unit' (db/hosted/baseline-manifest.ts). For CE-1 the correct value is the id of the immediately preceding drizzle unit at the implementer's base (at START_HEAD: ['0065_fib_sensitivity_model.sql']). CE-1 has NO second dependency: it creates a brand-new table and one nullable FK on organizations, both of which exist far earlier in the chain, and it enables RLS without referencing any helper function, so it needs no edge to 0031_rls_core.sql or to any policy unit. A dependency on 0031 would be a false edge.
FROZEN_DERIVATION_RULES.dml: 'none'. CE-1 is pure DDL. It inserts, updates and deletes nothing — the base's ORGANIZATION_FK.nullable_meaning is explicit that no writer sets the column at CE-1.
FROZEN_DERIVATION_RULES.managed: 'A-hosted-compatible'. CE-1 is CREATE TABLE / ADD COLUMN / ADD CONSTRAINT / CREATE INDEX plus two ALTER TABLE ... ROW LEVEL SECURITY statements on schema public, all of which managed Supabase grants `postgres`. It is NOT 'B-hosted-compatible-given-supabase' — that class is used where a unit depends on something the managed platform supplies (auth/storage schemas, auth.uid()), and CE-1 references neither auth nor storage.
FROZEN_DERIVATION_RULES.reapply: 'destructive-on-reapply'. The drizzle chain is forward-only; CREATE TABLE without IF NOT EXISTS fails on a second application. NOT 'idempotent' — that class is reserved for units whose every statement is guarded (the manifest verifier cross-checks the claim against the scan for policy units).
FROZEN_DERIVATION_RULES.managedNote: One reviewable sentence naming the CE-1 node, the objects created, and the RLS posture. FROZEN_DERIVATION_RULES.rollback: The PLAIN_DDL text is correct and should be used: applied with psql -1 so a failure inside the unit rolls the unit back whole; no reverse script, because the drizzle chain is forward-only and a partially advanced chain is recovered by DESTROY_AND_REPROVISION, not by hand.
FROZEN_DERIVATION_RULES.equivalentTo: ABSENT. That field exists only for the A2 policy units that repeat a migration's content. CE-1 is not one.
FROZEN_DERIVATION_RULES.expect: EXACTLY { rlsEnabledTableCount: 1 }. Every other field of BaselineExpectedScan defaults to the safe value and MUST be left unstated — the verifier spreads `...unit.expect` over a full set of zero/false defaults, so an unstated field is asserted to be safe rather than unchecked.

SCANNER_BEHAVIOUR_RE_DERIVED.securitySurfaceDigest_derivation: MEASURED: db/hosted/baseline-scanner.ts pushes into `securitySurface` in exactly two places — a CREATE POLICY predicate (line 350) and a SECURITY DEFINER function body (line 363). THEREFORE the field is OMITTED from `expect`, per the manifest's own stated convention: 'Omitted means the unit has no policy and no definer, and the verifier expects the digest of the empty string.' Writing the literal digest instead of omitting it would be legal but non-conventional; omitting it is the frozen instruction.
